case_title: MIS. HARYANA STATE COOP. SUPPLY AND MARKETING FEDERATION LTD. v. MIS. JAYAM TEXTILES & ANR.
statutory_provisions: Negotiable Instruments Act s.138, s.140; Penal Code s.420
trial_court_outcome: Complaints dismissed on grounds of lack of authorisation
neutral_facts: The appellant-federation supplied cotton bales to the respondents and issued four cheques to discharge their liability. However, all four cheques were returned unpaid by the bank for want of sufficient funds. The appellant-federation filed complaints under Sections 138 and 140 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 read with Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code. The complaints were dismissed by the Judicial Magistrate and the appeals were dismissed by the High Court solely on the ground that authorisation was not produced by the complainant-appellant. The appellant-federation claimed there was an authorisation from the Board of Directors, but it was not filed along with the complaint. The Supreme Court remitted the matter back to the Trial Court with a direction to conduct a fresh trial, taking into consideration the authorisation provided.
